presentation_summary: 69-year-old man with chronic tophaceous gout since 1980 had recurrent flares, then developed a protracted acute polyarticular gout attack.

The attack involved wrists, knees, ankles, right elbow, and first metatarsophalangeal joints and persisted for 3.5 months despite allopurinol, colchicine/NSAIDs during attacks, prednisone, and increased benzbromarone.
Serum uric acid was 3.7 mg/dL during the flare and fell to 2.2 mg/dL, showing that acute gout can persist despite low serum urate.

Right-knee arthrocentesis withdrew 40 mL low-viscosity turbid fluid with negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals, WBC 19,000/mm3 with 90% polymorphonuclear cells, and negative aerobic, anaerobic, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures.
Foot radiographs showed subchondral cysts and typical gout bone erosions; ESR was 75 mm/h and CRP was reported as 278.

outcome.clinical_course: After benzbromarone was split to 100 mg twice daily, polyarthritis progressively improved; within one month the patient walked normally, CRP and ESR normalized, prednisone was withdrawn, and no new attacks occurred for more than 18 months.

quality_warnings: Low serum urate during the flare is retained as evidence, because acute gout can persist with normal or low serum urate when tissue crystals remain.
Negative cultures are retained as observed microbiology; they do not imply that crystals would exclude infection in other cases.
